This puts the local +4.15 courtyard face at y=47.724, i.e. 0.145 mm off the north edge y=47.579, reproducing exactly the courtyard-to-edge offset the flown FC J12 (same HRO part) was built with. Destination window x 269.4-280.6 / y 46.6-57.3 is measured empty. After the move the new courtyard max y = 57.144, giving 1.14 mm to the R701/R702 courtyards (tops at 58.28) - above the 0.5 mm floor, no PM exception needed. Checklist rows that must still hold: J701 remains a fixed-anchor-class connector on the north edge with min pad copper to Edge.Cuts >= 0.2 mm (currently 1.771 mm, will become ~2.0 mm after the flip; re-measure); no courtyard overlap with R701/R702/C701/J703/SW701/SW702; the F.Cu USB corridor east of J703 (x 274.19-296.39, 22.20 mm free, y 50-89) stays unobstructed. After the move, re-verify which physical pad each of D+/D-/CC1/CC2 lands on: the 180 deg flip mirrors the pad row, so the net-to-pad assignment for R703/R704 (EMU_USB_DP/DM) and R701/R702 (CC) must be re-checked before routing - this is a verification step, not a placement change.

Verify each via individually against existing F.Cu heritage copper rather than assuming a uniform x: J9 SCL/SDA fit near x 222.2-223.3, J13.5/J13.6 need x 221.5-222.0 (the F.Cu free band at x = 222.8 stops at y = 122.8 against pads at 123.80/125.30), J2 not yet measured. BLOCKER PLM-02 (owner outline decision, changes plane topology - must be taken before routing): J12 (FC's own laptop USB-C, B.Cu, rot -90, courtyard x 217.845-227.355, y 73.235-83.965) opens +X into the new wing. An Edge.Cuts scan over x 224-246 / y 54-136 finds ZERO cutout - the board is solid from the old FC edge x=227.50 to x=296.44 across J12's full height. The plug shell occupies x 226.81-233.3 when seated and the overmold is up to 6.5 mm; the obstruction is the PCB itself, so L3 (2 mm part-height lane rule) does not help. Option (a): cut a relief slot through the wing at approximately x 228.5-241 / y 72.0-85.2 - measured free of parts on both sides - and accept the In1 GND-plane split plus the stitching-via cost around the slot. Option (b): record J12 as not-matable on FlatSat V1 in the build/ATP documentation and drive the FC over J703/J702 and the emulator's own J701 instead. Option (a) must be decided before routing because it changes the In1 plane.

Verified clear at the 3.35 mm keep-clear: (232.5, 50.5), (252.0, 140.0), (262.0, 50.0), (262.0, 140.0). Reserve (232.5, 50.5) and (252.0, 140.0) as the primaries; keep (262.0, 50/140) as fallbacks only, since that N-S channel is the wing's widest routing corridor. 3 fiducials, 1 mm copper / 2 mm mask opening, >= 3.35 mm clear of parts and of the H11/H12 annular rings.

NETCLASS (pre-routing setup): the project .kicad_pro currently defines only the Default class (0.2 clearance / 0.25 track / via 0.8/0.4) with no netclass_patterns - BenchPower and USB_EMU are not yet instantiated. Create them before routing, and at the same time (a) scope USB_EMU strictly to EMU_USB_DP/EMU_USB_DM per L5, i.e. beginning at R703/R704 and NOT at J701, whose pads carry Default-class Net-(J701-D+-PadA6)/Net-(J701-D--PadA7); (b) exclude the 3V3_EMU west branch to R602.2 from the blanket BenchPower 1.0 mm width (see routing_instructions); (c) add a local 0.45 mm pad / 0.20 mm drill via override for the U200 and U511 escape rings.
routing_instructions: LAYER BUDGET: In1.Cu is a single GND polygon x 139.8-298.5 / y 45.1-174.5 covering the whole grown board - keep it uncut under U200 (x 267-280, y 88-101) and under the entire USB corridor (x 274-276, y 50-89), and place stitching vias outside those two rectangles. Every heritage In2 pour stops at the Rev2 outline (x <= 231.14, y <= 141.87), so In2 is COMPLETELY EMPTY over the wing (x > 231.4) and the strip (y > 142.1). F.Cu and B.Cu already carry GND pours in the new area (wing x 232.0-295.5 / y 48.5-171.2 prio 1; strip x 144.3-232.0 / y 143.0-171.2 prio 2). Net effect: three usable signal layers over a solid plane in the extension, ZERO inside the 12 mm attachment band. Be generous in the extension, surgical in the band. Do not create any new pour inside the Rev2 outline.

ORDER OF WORK: (1) settle PLR-01 and PLR-02 (rule decisions) first; (2) hand-route all 37 L11 stubs on the pad's own layer and re-run tools/pcb/attachment_check.py - Freerouting will not respect the band and its output gets pruned anyway; (3) hand-route the USB pair end to end on F.Cu and fix it; (4) hand-route the U200 and U511 escapes with 0.45/0.20 vias and fix them; (5) only then release Freerouting on the remainder.

USB PAIR: run EMU_USB_DP/DM on F.Cu the whole way so the pair never leaves the In1 reference. Two vias per net at J701 are permitted and expected (Default class - the no-vias note applies only from R703/R704 onward); place them symmetrically about 1.5-2.0 mm south of the pad row at x ~ 274.3 and 275.7, y ~ 52.0-52.5, using 0.45/0.25 so D+ and D- see identical via counts. Then take the pair straight down the 22.20 mm free channel east of J703 at x ~ 274.5/275.0 for the full 38.5 mm run. Straight-line skew today is 0.04 mm. Accept the 1.800 mm taper at R703/R704 as an ordinary series-termination fan-in - do not move the resistors.

U200 ESCAPE: no track of any legal width fits between adjacent pads (0.200 mm gap vs 0.381 mm needed), so escape is strictly radial. The Default 0.8/0.4 via needs 1.054 mm of annulus and fails at U200's median (1.030) and everywhere at U511 (0.875-0.900) - use the 0.45/0.20 override (0.654 mm envelope) in both rings. 15 U200 pads sit at 0.520-0.541 mm annulus (QSPI 57-60 against C212, plus pins 17-21, 29, 30, 46) and take no in-line via at all: route them sideways into the 13 alleys of 0.890-1.160 mm first, then via down. Reserve the 1.160 mm north-row alley at x 273.165-274.325 for the QSPI group. DO NOT rotate U200 - 90 deg only improves the opposite-side pin count from 10 to 8 and costs the USB and QSPI placements.

In2 POPULATION: drop U200's ten opposite-side signals straight onto In2 and carry them under the package - TOP_SDA, TOP_SCL, CTL_USBBOOT, SWCLK, SWDIO, UART_TX, PYRO_INHIBIT_STATE, F5_SENSE, F1_SENSE, F4_SENSE. Add J703's eight signals to the same In2 population (3V3_EMU, EMU_UART_TX, EMU_UART_RX, EMU_GPIO_SPARE0, EMU_GPIO_SPARE1, FC_RESET, USBBOOT, WDT_DISABLE) - J703 is a fixed anchor and does not move, so In2 is the cheap mitigation for its 119 crossing incidences. Keep every In2 via for these nets clear of the F.Cu USB corridor and off U200's QFN pads (no via-in-pad on U200).

MAJOR PLR-06 (3V3_EMU and PYRO_INHIBIT_STATE): pour 3V3_EMU on In2 over x 265-296 / y 86-112 ONLY, at a priority below GND - that covers 24 of its 34 pads and kills roughly 90 of its 105 crossings. Route its single west branch to R602.2 (157.5, 158.6) as one 0.5 mm In2 track, not at the BenchPower 1.0 mm width: it feeds one indicator LED at a few mA. Route PYRO_INHIBIT_STATE (U200.35 -> R601.2, 129.4 mm, 50 crossings, the worst single edge on the board) on In2 through the same corridor. Both then stay out of the strip's F.Cu north band, whose narrowest points are 2.25 mm at x = 250 (TP401), 2.55 mm at x = 265 (TP511) and 3.09 mm at x = 220 (C315) - a single BenchPower track consumes 1.500 mm of that. DO NOT pour 3V3_EMU across the whole wing and strip: In2 is the extension's only unencumbered signal layer and is worth more as a routing layer than as a plane arm.

DECOUPLING GND VIAS (45 caps): C204, C209, C212 and C219 take a 0.50 mm via at 0.39 mm out (0.220 mm clearance); C213 and C217 take 0.60 mm; C206 and C216 clear an 0.8/0.4 by only 0.130 mm against a 0.127 mm floor - do not place their GND vias radially at all, drop them into the E-W lane at y 100.2-100.8, measured completely free across x 266.00-296.39.

U511 THERMAL: add a 3x3 array of 0.4/0.2 vias on U511's exposed pad at 0.9 mm pitch (0.25 mm margin to the 2.7 x 2.7 mm EP edge; B.Cu measured clear +/- 3 mm), and confirm JLCPCB's via-in-pad tenting/plugging capability at that pitch. Spread Q500/Q501 drain copper on B.Cu (clear for 3 mm). Leave U200's EP alone - its footprint is byte-identical to the flown FC U18.

EASY CORRIDORS (no special handling): face-column -> core, 33 signal nets across the x 266.4-268.9 gap, column free of parts for 94 mm of y (only obstacle R708 at x=259, y 76.67-77.31) - 33 tracks at 0.45 mm pitch need 14.85 mm of 94. Core -> bench I/O: y = 100.5, 106.0 and 110.0 each free across the full 30.39 mm width. Strip BenchPower runs J500 -> Q500/Q501/U500 -> JP602-607 and J400/J401 -> F400/F401 -> D400/D401 -> JP400/JP401 have 4.06-15.42 mm free y-bands against the 1.50 mm a 1.0 mm track needs.

GATE EXPECTATIONS on the first attachment_check.py run after stub routing: expect a handful of same-net false positives that are electrically fine - the VSOLAR stub at J11.1 (the heritage VSOLAR daisy chain on F.Cu, x 220.81-222.43 / y 88.07-125.15, touches that pad) and the six face stubs whose own heritage traces leave the same pads. Even if the relief slot is cut, a fixture that allows a laptop into J12 simultaneously with the top-side connectors needs open underside access - the board cannot rest flat on a solid plate. Document the required standoff height and underside access. J12 is heritage-frozen (L4).

PLM-06 (note, stage 6+ watch item): J510's receptacle face sits 2.36 mm behind the south board edge versus the flown FC J12's 0.64 mm. Plugs seat fine (6.5 mm shell against 2.36 mm recess) and J510 is a fixed anchor of charger_bq25886, unmoved bit-for-bit across PM rounds 3-5 - no change now. Log the margin so it can be revisited if a thicker boot or strain relief is ever specified.

PLM-13 (note, first-article inspection): the wire-entry face of the Phoenix MKDS 1,5/2-5.08 (1715721) at J400/J401/J500 could not be confirmed against a dimensional drawing (Farnell timeout, DigiKey and Phoenix 403, KiCad 3D model featureless).
